source_text: Meta-analyses confirm this effect, attributing it to the foreskin's vulnerability to microtears and epithelial disruption during intercourse, which increases HIV entry points; the protective estimate holds in high-prevalence settings but requires consideration of behavioral and epidemiological context for generalizability.
